definition: Haloperidol is a phenyl-piperidinyl-butyrophenone medication used mainly for schizophrenia and other psychoses. It is also used for schizoaffective and delusional disorders, Tourette syndrome, and some movement-related conditions, and it can help control severe nausea and persistent hiccups.

provenance.scope: Source record D006220; pinned source text

reasons: "Severe nausea" is not supported by the packet; the packet says haloperidol is a potent antiemetic and is used for intractable hiccups, but it does not specify severe nausea.
"Some movement-related conditions" is an unsupported generalization beyond the packet’s named uses (ballism and the chorea of Huntington disease).

The definition is for a medication (haloperidol) and describes indications/treatment uses rather than providing a term definition in the “diagnosis” field (the term is not itself a diagnostic category).
The packet does not specify “severe nausea” (it only states it is a “potent antiemetic”).
The packet does not specify “persistent” hiccups (it states it is used for “intractable HICCUPS,” which is not the same wording/sense as “persistent”).
